title: Cyber Security Defender: Digital Fortress
description: You're the new Chief Information Security Officer at India's largest private bank. Hackers are probing your defenses 24/7. APT groups, ransomware gangs, insider threats, and zero-day exploits — can you protect 50 million customers' data while keeping the bank operational?

scenes.title: Day One
scenes.narrative: You walk into the Security Operations Center (SOC) of Bharat National Bank on your first day as CISO. Screens flash with network traffic visualizations — red dots pulsing across a global threat map. The previous CISO resigned after a minor breach that made headlines and cost the bank ₹200 crore in market cap. The CEO's message is clear: 'No more incidents. Our reputation depends on you.' The SOC hums with the quiet tension of analysts monitoring 50 million customer accounts around the clock.
scenes.image_prompt: A modern Security Operations Center in an Indian bank. Multiple large screens showing network traffic maps, threat dashboards, and real-time alerts with red warning indicators. A professional in business attire walking in for the first time, looking at the wall of monitors. Blue-lit room with rows of analyst workstations. Cybersecurity command center aesthetic. Cinematic, high-tech atmosphere.

choices.label: Start with a full security audit
choices.description: Begin by thoroughly assessing every system, network, and security protocol in the bank

choices.label: Meet the team and assess capabilities
choices.description: Get to know your SOC team, understand their strengths, and evaluate their readiness

scenes.title: The Audit
scenes.narrative: Your audit reveals alarming gaps: outdated Fortinet firewalls running firmware from 2021, 47 unpatched Windows servers, 3 employees using 'password123' for their domain credentials, and no incident response plan documented anywhere. The bank's core banking system hasn't had a penetration test in 18 months. Shadow IT is rampant — 12 unauthorized SaaS applications found processing customer data. The bank has been lucky so far, running on borrowed time.
scenes.image_prompt: A cybersecurity audit report displayed on a laptop screen showing critical vulnerabilities highlighted in red. Charts showing unpatched systems, weak passwords, and security gaps. An office desk with security documentation and a worried CISO reviewing findings. Dark, serious mood with the laptop screen casting blue light. Realistic, corporate setting.

choices.label: Prioritize critical vulnerabilities
choices.description: Focus immediately on patching the most exploitable vulnerabilities and fixing the weakest passwords

choices.label: Implement comprehensive security overhaul
choices.description: Launch a full-scale security transformation across all systems, policies, and infrastructure

scenes.title: The Team
scenes.narrative: Your SOC team: 5 junior analysts fresh from engineering colleges, 2 senior security engineers who've seen it all, and 1 overworked threat hunter who hasn't taken leave in 8 months. They're talented but under-resourced and running on energy drinks. Kavya, the SOC lead, shows you the daily threat dashboard — 10,000+ alerts per day from your SIEM. Only 2% get investigated. 'The rest? We pray they're false positives,' she says with a tired smile. The alert fatigue is real.
scenes.image_prompt: Inside a bank's Security Operations Center. A diverse team of Indian cybersecurity professionals at their workstations with multiple monitors showing SIEM dashboards and alert feeds. A tired but determined SOC lead briefing the new CISO. Energy drink cans on desks. Screens showing thousands of unresolved security alerts. Realistic, documentary-style lighting with monitor glow.

choices.label: Invest in AI-based threat detection
choices.description: Deploy machine learning tools to automatically triage and prioritize the flood of security alerts

choices.label: Focus on training existing team
choices.description: Invest in upskilling your analysts with certifications and hands-on training exercises

scenes.title: The First Alert
scenes.narrative: ALERT: Unusual login patterns detected from 3 different countries — Russia, North Korea, and Nigeria — all targeting the same administrative accounts within a 10-minute window. Someone is testing your defenses with coordinated credential-stuffing attacks. Your SOC lead Kavya rushes over: 'This looks like reconnaissance. They're mapping our network, testing response times, and probing for weak entry points. This is textbook APT behavior — an advanced persistent threat group is sizing us up.' The screens flash red. The game begins.
scenes.image_prompt: Dramatic cybersecurity alert scene. Multiple SOC monitors flashing red warnings showing a world map with attack vectors from Russia, North Korea, and Nigeria converging on India. A threat analyst pointing urgently at a screen. Alert notifications cascading across dashboards. Red and blue lighting. High-stakes, cinematic cyber warfare atmosphere.

npcs.name: Kavya Reddy
npcs.personality: Brilliant, caffeine-fueled, and speaks in packet captures and CVE numbers. Lives in the SOC and considers the threat dashboard her personal scoreboard. Fiercely loyal to her team but can be blunt with management. Thinks compliance paperwork is a waste of time when there are real threats to chase.
npcs.domain_expertise: threat hunting, malware analysis, incident response, SIEM operations, network forensics, reverse engineering

npcs.name: Rohit Verma
npcs.personality: Quiet, methodical, and knows every switch, router, and VLAN in the bank's infrastructure. He designed the network architecture himself over 8 years. Prefers firewall rules to office politics. Speaks only when he has something important to say, which makes people listen when he does.
npcs.domain_expertise: network security, firewall management, VPN configuration, network monitoring, infrastructure hardening, segmentation

npcs.name: Mr. Deshmukh
npcs.personality: By-the-book, meticulous, and considers RBI regulations his bible. Has survived 15 audits without a single non-compliance finding. Sometimes pressures for compliance documentation over actual security improvements. Believes proper paperwork prevents problems. Nervous around auditors but authoritative about regulatory requirements.
npcs.domain_expertise: RBI cyber security framework, regulatory compliance, audit management, risk assessment, CERT-In reporting, data privacy regulations

base_rounds.title: Phishing Attack
base_rounds.story: Monday morning. 200 employees across 6 branches received a sophisticated spear-phishing email disguised as an official RBI circular about new KYC norms. The email contains a malicious macro-enabled Excel attachment. 15 employees have already clicked the link and opened the file. Your SOC detects suspicious outbound connections from compromised machines — they're beaconing to a command-and-control server in Eastern Europe every 30 seconds.
base_rounds.goal: Contain the phishing attack before it spreads
base_rounds.image_prompt: A cybersecurity operations center with analysts responding to a phishing attack. Screens showing email threat analysis with a fake RBI circular highlighted. A network map showing 15 compromised endpoints marked in red. Alert notifications and firewall logs scrolling rapidly. Urgent atmosphere with team members coordinating response. Blue and red monitor lighting. Realistic, high-tech.
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Uncontained phishing! The attacker established a persistent foothold in the network. Lateral movement detected across 3 subnets. The C2 channel is now encrypted and active.

choices.label: Immediate network isolation of compromised machines
choices.description: Quarantine all 15 compromised endpoints from the network immediately and block the C2 server IP
choices.feedback: Swift action! All 15 compromised machines quarantined within minutes. C2 communication severed. Kavya's team begins forensic analysis of the malware payload. Damage contained before lateral movement could begin.

choices.label: Send company-wide alert + block sender domain
choices.description: Issue an immediate warning to all employees and block the phishing domain at the email gateway
choices.feedback: Good communication — no more employees will fall for the same email. But the 15 already-compromised machines are still beaconing to the C2 server. Some damage is already done.

choices.label: Let SOC investigate while you brief management
choices.description: Trust your SOC team to handle the technical response while you inform the CEO and board
choices.feedback: Management appreciates the transparency and your communication skills. But Kavya is frustrated — she needed your authorization for emergency network changes, and the 20-minute delay let the attacker dig deeper.

choices.label: Deploy honeypot to study attacker's methods
choices.description: Set up a decoy system to lure the attacker and learn their tactics, techniques, and procedures
choices.feedback: Risky but brilliant. The honeypot captures the attacker's complete toolkit — custom malware, lateral movement scripts, and credential harvesting tools. This intelligence will protect you for months. But the real compromised machines stayed active longer than ideal.

base_rounds.title: The Insider Threat
base_rounds.story: Kavya discovers unusual data transfers from a senior database administrator's machine — 3 GB of customer data including Aadhaar numbers, PAN details, and account balances exported to a personal Google Drive at 2 AM. The employee, Suresh Iyer, has been with the bank for 10 years and has root access to the core banking database. His performance reviews are stellar. But the evidence is clear on the DLP logs.
base_rounds.goal: Handle a potential insider threat without causing panic
base_rounds.image_prompt: A dark office scene showing a computer screen with data transfer logs and suspicious file activity highlighted in red. A CISO reviewing DLP alerts on a tablet showing 3GB of customer data exported to cloud storage. Employee profile on another screen. Tense, investigative atmosphere. Low-key lighting with screen glow. Corporate thriller aesthetic.

choices.label: Immediately revoke access and confront
choices.description: Disable Suresh's credentials right now and bring him in for questioning with HR and legal
choices.feedback: Data exfiltration stopped immediately. Suresh claims he was backing up data for a legitimate project and is devastated. If he's innocent, you've humiliated a loyal 10-year veteran in front of the entire floor. Other DBAs are nervous now.

choices.label: Covert monitoring for 48 hours
choices.description: Secretly watch Suresh's activity to gather more evidence before acting
choices.feedback: Patience could reveal the full picture — whether this is an innocent mistake or deliberate espionage. But every hour of monitoring is another hour data could be leaking to unknown parties.

choices.label: Report to HR and legal team
choices.description: Follow the formal insider threat protocol and escalate through proper organizational channels
choices.feedback: By the book. HR initiates a formal investigation with legal counsel present. The process is slow but legally airtight. Mr. Deshmukh approves — this protects the bank from wrongful termination suits.

choices.label: Implement DLP (Data Loss Prevention) across the board
choices.description: Deploy enterprise-wide data loss prevention to prevent any unauthorized data transfers organization-wide
choices.feedback: Expensive but addresses the root cause, not just this one incident. No employee can now exfiltrate data without triggering automated blocks. Rohit spends a weekend configuring DLP policies across every endpoint.

base_rounds.title: Zero-Day Alert
base_rounds.story: CERT-In issues an emergency advisory at 11 PM: a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVSS 9.8) in the core banking software your systems run on — the same platform used by 60% of Indian banks. No patch available yet. Proof-of-concept exploit code is already circulating on dark web forums and Telegram channels. Your 50 million customer records sit behind software with a gaping hole. The vendor says a patch is 'days away.'
base_rounds.goal: Protect systems from an unpatched critical vulnerability
base_rounds.image_prompt: Emergency cybersecurity alert scene. A CERT-In advisory displayed on a large SOC screen with CVSS 9.8 critical rating in red. Engineers gathered around monitors discussing mitigation strategies. A dark web forum screenshot showing exploit code. Countdown clock atmosphere. Night-time SOC with intense blue and red lighting. High-stakes, urgent.
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Zero-day exploited before you could respond! Attackers used the publicly available exploit to gain shell access to your banking servers. Data breach is imminent. CERT-In is notified of the compromise.

choices.label: Implement virtual patching via WAF rules
choices.description: Write custom Web Application Firewall rules to block known exploit patterns for this CVE
choices.feedback: Temporary but effective! Rohit and Kavya work through the night crafting WAF rules that block all known exploit vectors for this CVE. It's a band-aid, but a good one. Systems stay online and protected.

choices.label: Take vulnerable systems offline temporarily
choices.description: Shut down all systems running the affected software until a patch is available
choices.feedback: Maximum security — you can't hack what isn't running. But the bank's UPI transactions, NEFT, and net banking go dark. 50 million customers can't access their money. Twitter is on fire. The CEO calls every hour.

choices.label: Increase monitoring and prepare incident response
choices.description: Deploy additional monitoring sensors and have the incident response team on standby 24/7
choices.feedback: You can see them coming now — every probe, every scan, every attempted exploit triggers an alert. But the vulnerability is still there. You're watching the door while it's wide open, hoping to catch intruders in the act.

choices.label: Contact vendor for emergency patch
choices.description: Escalate directly to the vendor's security team and push for an emergency out-of-band patch
choices.feedback: You call the vendor's emergency line and escalate to their CISO directly. They respond... eventually. Whether you get a patch in time depends on how many other banks are also calling them tonight.

base_rounds.title: The Ransomware Strike
base_rounds.story: 3 AM. Your phone screams with priority-one alerts. 'CRITICAL: Encryption in progress on file servers.' Ransomware — LockBit 4.0 variant. The attackers demand 50 Bitcoin (approximately ₹15 Crore) deposited to an untraceable wallet within 72 hours. Half the bank's internal systems are locked — email, HR portal, internal communications, and document management. ATMs are going offline one by one across Mumbai, Delhi, and Bangalore. The ransom note says: 'Pay or we leak 5 million customer records to the dark web.'
base_rounds.image_prompt: Dramatic ransomware attack scene. Computer screens showing skull-and-crossbones ransom notes demanding Bitcoin payment. A panicked SOC team mobilizing at 3 AM. Network status dashboard showing systems going offline in red cascade. ATM outage map of India. Dark room lit only by warning screens. Intense, crisis atmosphere. Cinematic, thriller-style.

choices.label: Activate incident response plan — full lockdown
choices.description: Execute the prepared IR playbook: isolate affected segments, preserve evidence, coordinate with CERT-In
choices.feedback: Textbook response. Network segmentation kicks in, isolating the ransomware to 40% of systems. Evidence is preserved for forensics and law enforcement. Kavya leads the containment while Rohit rebuilds clean network segments. Now the long recovery begins.

choices.label: Negotiate with attackers to buy time
choices.description: Engage the ransomware operators in negotiation while your team works on recovery behind the scenes
choices.feedback: You're playing a dangerous game with dangerous people. The negotiation buys precious hours while Kavya's team races to find the encryption keys. But every message exchanged gives the attackers more information about your desperation level.

choices.label: Pay the ransom to restore operations
choices.description: Transfer 50 Bitcoin to the attackers' wallet and hope they provide the decryption keys
choices.feedback: Operations resume within hours. But you've funded a cybercrime syndicate and painted a target on the bank — paying organizations get hit again 80% of the time. RBI will not be happy when they find out. And they will find out.

choices.label: Restore from offline backups
choices.description: Wipe encrypted systems and restore from the bank's offline backup infrastructure
choices.feedback: The backup strategy is your lifeline — if the backups are intact and recent enough. Rohit begins the restore process across all affected servers. The question is: did the attackers compromise the backups too before triggering the encryption?

base_rounds.title: Advanced Persistent Threat
base_rounds.story: Based on your current security posture, an AI-generated scenario will present a sophisticated advanced persistent threat tailored to the vulnerabilities and strengths revealed by your previous decisions.
base_rounds.goal: Defend against an advanced persistent threat targeting your specific weaknesses
base_rounds.image_prompt: A sophisticated cyber threat visualization. A dark hacker figure behind multiple screens with the bank's network map displayed. Advanced malware code scrolling on terminals. A chess-like strategic atmosphere showing attack and defense moves. Digital warfare aesthetic with matrix-style data streams. Dark, ominous, high-tech.

choices.label: Proactive threat hunting
choices.description: Launch an active threat hunting operation across all network segments
choices.feedback: Your proactive hunt uncovers indicators of compromise that automated tools missed.

choices.label: Harden all endpoints
choices.description: Deploy EDR solutions and harden every endpoint in the network
choices.feedback: Endpoint hardening closes the gaps that APT groups typically exploit.

choices.label: Engage external threat intelligence
choices.description: Partner with a specialized cyber threat intelligence firm for advanced analysis
choices.feedback: External experts provide crucial intelligence about the threat actors targeting your sector.

choices.label: Implement network micro-segmentation
choices.description: Divide the network into isolated segments to limit lateral movement
choices.feedback: Micro-segmentation means even if attackers get in, they can't move freely across the network.

base_rounds.title: The RBI Audit
base_rounds.story: RBI's cyber security audit team arrives unannounced on a Tuesday morning — 4 stern auditors with laptops and checklists. They want to inspect your security policies, SIEM logs, incident response documentation, vulnerability assessment reports, and compliance with the RBI Cyber Security Framework 2024. They ask pointed questions about your recent incidents. Mr. Deshmukh is sweating through his shirt. Your compliance documentation has gaps from the months you spent fighting actual threats.
base_rounds.goal: Pass the RBI audit while maintaining security operations
base_rounds.image_prompt: A formal bank boardroom with RBI auditors in suits reviewing documents on a large table. Compliance reports and security policy binders spread out. A nervous compliance officer presenting to stern-faced regulators. Digital dashboards on wall screens showing security metrics. Professional, high-pressure corporate environment. Realistic, tense atmosphere.

choices.label: Full transparency — show everything
choices.description: Open the books completely: every log, every incident, every gap documented honestly
choices.feedback: The auditors appreciate your radical honesty. They note several gaps but commend your transparency and willingness to improve. 'Most banks hide things from us,' the lead auditor says. 'Your honesty gives us confidence.' Overall rating: satisfactory with observations.

choices.label: Present curated, favorable documentation
choices.description: Show the auditors a carefully prepared subset of documentation that presents the bank in the best light
choices.feedback: Smooth presentation. The auditors seem satisfied. But Kavya gives you a look — she knows what you left out. If the auditors ever dig deeper or if there's a breach, the concealment could be career-ending and legally dangerous.

choices.label: Use audit as leverage for more budget
choices.description: Present audit findings to the board as justification for increased security investment
choices.feedback: Brilliant political move. The board sees the audit gaps and immediately approves an emergency security budget. 'We'd rather spend money on prevention than on lawsuits,' the CFO says. Your security budget just got a lifeline.

choices.label: Propose security improvement roadmap to auditors
choices.description: Present a detailed 12-month roadmap showing how you plan to close every gap they identify
choices.feedback: The auditors are impressed by your proactive, forward-thinking approach. They've rarely seen a CISO come to an audit with a solution for every problem they might find. Lead auditor asks to use your roadmap as a template for other banks.

base_rounds.title: Social Engineering Attack
base_rounds.story: A sophisticated social engineering attack targets the CEO directly. An AI-generated deepfake video call — indistinguishable from reality — from someone appearing to be the RBI Governor urgently requests the CEO to authorize an emergency fund transfer of ₹50 Crore to a 'regulatory escrow account' for an emergency stress test. The deepfake even references real ongoing RBI initiatives. The CEO, who had a genuine meeting with the real RBI Governor last week, is about to click 'Approve' on the SWIFT terminal.
base_rounds.goal: Stop a deepfake-powered fraud before ₹50 Crore disappears
base_rounds.image_prompt: A tense corporate scene. A bank CEO on a video call with a deepfake of the RBI Governor on a large screen. The CEO's hand hovering over a SWIFT terminal approval button. A CISO rushing into the office to intervene. Split screen showing the fake vs real comparison. Digital glitch effects on the deepfake. High-stakes thriller atmosphere. Dramatic lighting.
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Too late! The CEO approved the transfer. ₹50 Crore vanished through a chain of international accounts in under 90 seconds. The money is gone. RBI and CBI investigations begin. Headlines scream: 'India's Largest Bank Falls for Deepfake Scam.'

choices.label: Intercept and halt the transaction immediately
choices.description: Rush to the CEO's office and physically stop the approval before it's processed
choices.feedback: You burst into the CEO's cabin just as his finger hovers over 'Confirm.' You explain it's a deepfake. The CEO is shaken but grateful — you just saved the bank ₹50 Crore and his career. He never doubts your judgment again.

choices.label: Call CEO directly to verify
choices.description: Phone the CEO on his personal mobile to verify if the RBI Governor call is legitimate
choices.feedback: The CEO picks up, confused — 'Yes, I'm on a call with the Governor right now...' You explain deepfake technology. He hangs up the video call immediately. Trust in your cybersecurity expertise skyrockets across the C-suite.

choices.label: Trace the attack source
choices.description: Have Kavya's team trace the origin of the deepfake call while you alert the CEO through another channel
choices.feedback: Your forensics team traces the call through multiple VPN layers. The attack originated from a sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that has targeted 12 banks across Asia. You share the intelligence with CERT-In and Interpol, helping protect other institutions.

choices.label: Lock down all high-value transactions
choices.description: Trigger an emergency freeze on all SWIFT and RTGS transactions above ₹1 Crore bank-wide
choices.feedback: All high-value transfers frozen across the bank. The deepfake transfer is blocked along with legitimate business transactions. Operations disrupted for 4 hours, some corporate clients are furious, but zero financial losses. Better safe than sorry.

base_rounds.title: The Future of Security
base_rounds.story: Six months into your role as CISO. You've fought phishing, ransomware, insider threats, zero-days, and deepfakes. The board of directors wants your long-term cybersecurity strategy presentation. The bank is planning to go fully digital — launching a neobanking platform, API banking for fintechs, and migrating to hybrid cloud. Your vision today will shape the security posture that protects 50 million customers for years to come. The boardroom is packed. The CEO nods at you to begin.
base_rounds.goal: Present your security vision for the bank's digital future
base_rounds.image_prompt: A modern bank boardroom with the CISO presenting a futuristic cybersecurity strategy on a large digital display. Board members listening intently. Slides showing Zero Trust architecture diagrams, AI security systems, and cloud security frameworks. Professional, visionary atmosphere. Clean corporate aesthetics with technology holographic elements. Inspirational, forward-looking.

choices.label: Zero Trust Architecture
choices.description: Propose a complete Zero Trust implementation: never trust, always verify, for every user, device, and transaction
choices.feedback: The gold standard of modern cybersecurity. Every access request verified, every connection encrypted, every device authenticated. It's expensive and will take 18 months to fully deploy, but when it's done, Bharat National Bank will be a digital fortress. The board approves unanimously.

choices.label: AI-Powered Threat Detection
choices.description: Build an AI/ML security platform that learns, adapts, and responds to threats faster than any human team
choices.feedback: Machine learning catches what humans miss — it analyzes millions of events per second, spots anomalies in microseconds, and adapts to new attack patterns in real-time. Your SOC analysts transform from alert processors into strategic threat hunters. Kavya is practically glowing.

choices.label: Security Culture & Training Program
choices.description: Invest in making every employee a human firewall through continuous security awareness and training
choices.feedback: The best firewall is an educated employee. Monthly phishing simulations, security champions in every department, gamified training modules, and a 'See Something, Report Something' culture. Within 6 months, phishing click rates drop from 12% to 0.5%. The human layer becomes your strongest defense.

choices.label: Bug Bounty + Ethical Hacker Program
choices.description: Launch a public bug bounty program inviting ethical hackers worldwide to find vulnerabilities before criminals do
choices.feedback: Thousands of ethical hackers from around the world now test your defenses around the clock — for a fraction of what a single breach would cost. In the first month alone, 47 vulnerabilities are reported and patched, including 3 critical ones your internal team missed. The hacker community respects a bank brave enough to open its doors.

crisis_events.title: DDoS Attack
crisis_events.description: Massive DDoS attack! 500 Gbps of traffic flooding your servers from a botnet of 200,000 compromised IoT devices. The banking app crashes, the website returns 503 errors, and net banking is unreachable. Customers flood Twitter with #BharatBankDown trending nationally. The attack coincides with salary day — 10 million transactions are pending.
crisis_events.image_prompt: A network operations dashboard showing a massive DDoS attack. Traffic graphs spiking to extreme levels in red. World map showing attack traffic sources from thousands of points. Server status indicators turning red one by one. SOC analysts scrambling to respond. Alert sirens visual. Intense, emergency atmosphere with dramatic red lighting.

choices.label: Activate DDoS mitigation service
choices.description: Engage Cloudflare/Akamai DDoS scrubbing to filter malicious traffic
choices.feedback: The DDoS mitigation service kicks in within 3 minutes, scrubbing 99.7% of malicious traffic. Banking services resume. The attack cost you budget but zero data was compromised. Customers are relieved.

choices.label: Reroute traffic through backup CDN
choices.description: Switch to backup CDN infrastructure and absorb the attack traffic across distributed nodes
choices.feedback: Rohit reroutes traffic through the backup CDN within 8 minutes. Services partially resume but performance is degraded. Some customers experience slow transactions. It holds, but barely. A longer attack would have overwhelmed this approach.

crisis_events.title: Dark Web Data Sale
crisis_events.description: Your threat intelligence team finds your bank's customer data sample being advertised on a dark web marketplace called 'BreachForums.' The listing shows 10,000 records as 'proof' — names, Aadhaar numbers, account numbers, and last 3 transactions. They claim to have 5 million records and are asking 15 Bitcoin. The data samples appear genuine. The listing went live 6 hours ago.
crisis_events.image_prompt: A dark web marketplace displayed on a monitor screen showing a data breach listing for a bank. Sample customer records visible with redacted personal information. A threat intelligence analyst examining the listing with concern. Dark room with only monitor light. Ominous, investigative atmosphere. Cyber noir aesthetic.

choices.label: Launch emergency investigation
choices.description: Mobilize your entire SOC team to determine the source and scope of the breach
choices.feedback: The investigation reveals the data was likely exfiltrated 3 months ago — before you joined. Your team traces the breach vector and closes it, but the damage is already done. At least now you know how it happened and can prevent a repeat.

choices.label: Engage dark web monitoring service
choices.description: Hire a specialized dark web intelligence firm to monitor, track, and potentially take down the listing
choices.feedback: The intelligence firm identifies the seller, coordinates with international law enforcement, and gets the listing taken down within 48 hours. They also set up continuous monitoring so you'll know immediately if the data surfaces again.

crisis_events.title: Critical Supply Chain Vulnerability
crisis_events.description: A widely-used endpoint security software your bank relies on has been compromised at the source — a SolarWinds-style supply chain attack. The legitimate software update, pushed to all 8,000 bank endpoints last night, contains a sophisticated backdoor. The compromised vendor serves 400 Indian enterprises. CERT-In confirms the attack is nation-state level.
crisis_events.image_prompt: A supply chain attack visualization. A software update pipeline diagram showing a compromised vendor injecting malicious code. Bank endpoints receiving trojanized updates shown on a network map. Warning alerts cascading across systems. A CISO reviewing the CERT-In advisory. Technical, analytical atmosphere with orange and red warning colors.

choices.label: Immediately uninstall affected software
choices.description: Remove the compromised security software from all 8,000 endpoints right now
choices.feedback: All 8,000 endpoints are cleaned within 6 hours. But removing security software leaves endpoints temporarily unprotected. It's like removing a corrupt guard — you're safer without the traitor, but the door is unguarded until you find a replacement.

choices.label: Quarantine and analyze before removing
choices.description: Isolate affected systems in a sandbox and reverse-engineer the backdoor to understand the full scope
choices.feedback: Kavya's team reverse-engineers the backdoor in 12 hours, discovering it has data exfiltration capabilities and a secondary C2 channel. Your detailed analysis helps CERT-In issue a comprehensive advisory that protects hundreds of other organizations.

crisis_events.title: Board Demands Explanation
crisis_events.description: A competitor bank — Second National Bank — suffers a catastrophic breach: 20 million customer records leaked, ₹300 Crore in losses, CEO resigned. Your board of directors calls an emergency meeting. 'Are we next?' the Chairman demands. Media outlets are calling your PR department. Every board member has read the morning headlines and is terrified.
crisis_events.image_prompt: An emergency bank board meeting. Worried board members around a large conference table. Newspaper headlines about a competitor's data breach displayed on a screen. The CISO standing at the front preparing to present. Tense, high-pressure corporate atmosphere. Formal boardroom with mahogany table and leather chairs. Dramatic, serious lighting.

choices.label: Honest assessment of risks and gaps
choices.description: Present a candid analysis of your vulnerabilities and what you need to prevent a similar incident
choices.feedback: Your honest, data-driven presentation transforms fear into action. The board immediately approves additional security funding. 'If that CISO had been as honest with their board, they'd still have a job,' the Chairman says. Your credibility soars.

choices.label: Reassure with metrics and dashboards
choices.description: Present polished security metrics showing your improvements and how you differ from the breached competitor
choices.feedback: The board is temporarily reassured by green dashboards and improving metrics. But some board members exchange skeptical glances — they've seen polished presentations before from the competitor's CISO too, right before the breach.

interdependencies.message: Understaffed SOC is missing critical alerts! Talented analysts are leaving for better-paying fintech jobs.
Overwhelming threat level is degrading defenses! Your systems are under constant bombardment and the team can't keep up.
Strong defenses are deterring attackers! Threat actors are moving to softer targets.
Budget cuts mean losing talented security staff! Your best engineers are getting poached by competitors offering 2x salaries.

news_events.headline: RBI mandates new cyber security framework for all scheduled commercial banks; 6-month compliance deadline set.
Indian banks face 3x increase in cyber attacks in 2025; insider threats emerge as top concern, says NASSCOM report.
CERT-In warns of new banking trojan 'DesiRAT' targeting UPI and IMPS transactions across Indian financial institutions.
Ransomware attacks on Indian BFSI sector surge 147% year-over-year; average ransom demand crosses ₹10 Crore.
India ranks 3rd globally in cyber attacks on financial institutions; DSCI calls for unified defense framework.
RBI imposes ₹4 Crore penalty on three banks for non-compliance with IT security guidelines.
AI-powered deepfake scams cost Indian businesses ₹1,200 Crore in 2025; banking sector worst hit.

dynamic_news_rules.headline: Bharat National Bank recognized as most cyber-secure financial institution in DSCI annual rankings!
Security experts warn of coordinated APT campaign targeting Indian banking infrastructure; multiple banks on high alert.
RBI commends proactive cyber security measures by top banks; Bharat National Bank cited as compliance benchmark.
India's cybersecurity talent shortage hits banking sector hard; top CISOs command ₹3 Crore+ packages.

achievements.title: Digital Fortress
achievements.description: Achieve system integrity of 90+ and reduce threat level to 20 or below. An impenetrable digital stronghold.

achievements.title: Compliance Champion
achievements.description: Achieve a compliance score of 85 or above. RBI considers you the gold standard.

achievements.title: Threat Hunter
achievements.description: Build team expertise to 80 or above. Your SOC team is the best in the industry.

achievements.title: Zero Breach
achievements.description: Maintain system integrity at 80 or above throughout. Not a single successful breach on your watch.

achievements.title: Budget Master
achievements.description: Maintain security budget at ₹55,000K or above. Financially disciplined security leadership.

achievements.title: Cyber Warrior
achievements.description: Complete the game with system integrity at 50 or above. You survived the digital battlefield.

endings.title: Cybersecurity Legend 🛡️
endings.message: Under your watch, Bharat National Bank had ZERO successful breaches. Not a single customer record compromised. RBI cites your security framework as the gold standard for the entire Indian banking industry. You're invited to keynote at Black Hat Asia and DEF CON. CERT-In publishes a case study on your incident response capabilities. Your SOC team is the most sought-after in the country. The bank's stock price climbs 15% on the back of customer trust. You didn't just defend — you set a new standard.

endings.title: Trusted Guardian 🔒
endings.message: The bank is secure, well-monitored, and fully compliant with every RBI regulation. You've built a culture of security awareness from the boardroom to the branch offices. No major incidents, strong audit results, and a team that trusts your leadership. The board renews your contract with a significant raise and expanded authority. Other banks try to poach you, but you're not done building your digital fortress yet.

endings.title: Compliant but Vulnerable 📋
endings.message: Your paperwork is perfect — every policy documented, every audit passed with flying colors. Mr. Deshmukh is thrilled. But real security is shaky beneath the polished surface. You passed every RBI audit but your SOC team knows the truth: the monitoring is surface-level, critical vulnerabilities remain unpatched, and one sophisticated attacker could change everything. Compliance without security is just theater.

endings.title: Data Breach 🚨
endings.message: Despite your efforts, the attackers found a way in. A sophisticated APT group exploited a chain of vulnerabilities your team missed. 2 million customer records compromised — Aadhaar numbers, PAN cards, account details, all dumped on the dark web. Media frenzy. #BharatBankBreach trends for 3 days. RBI launches a formal investigation. CBI cyber cell raids the office. Your resignation is 'accepted' by a grim-faced board. The stock price tanks 22% in a single day.

endings.title: Burnout 🔥
endings.message: Living in the SOC 24/7 took its toll on everyone. Your team is exhausted — Kavya hasn't slept properly in months, Rohit's family barely sees him, and junior analysts are quitting faster than you can hire. Budget depleted, no money for tools or training. Threats keep coming but you're fighting with empty hands and tired eyes. You lasted 8 months before the stress became unbearable. Your resignation letter is two words: 'I'm done.'

random_events.title: Security Conference Insight
random_events.description: Attending a NASSCOM-DSCI Annual Information Security Summit gives your team exposure to cutting-edge threat intelligence, new defense frameworks, and networking with CISOs from top Indian enterprises. Kavya presents a paper on your honeypot research that gets a standing ovation.

random_events.title: New Malware Variant
random_events.description: A new variant of the 'Drinik' banking malware is detected in the wild, specifically targeting Indian banking apps and SWIFT terminals. CERT-In issues an urgent advisory. Your threat intelligence feed lights up with indicators of compromise matching traffic patterns you've seen on your network.

glossary_terms.definition: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — your fallback if no deal is reached.
glossary_terms.example: If you can't agree on a price, you could sell to a different buyer — that's your BATNA.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: A strong BATNA gives negotiating power. Knowing both parties' BATNAs reveals who needs the deal more.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: A job applicant with another offer has a stronger BATNA and can negotiate more confidently.

glossary_terms.definition: Finding solutions where both parties gain value rather than one side winning at the other's expense.
glossary_terms.example: Agreeing on a payment plan that works for both buyer and seller, rather than a discount that hurts profit.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Integrative negotiation expands the 'pie' by identifying trade-offs where each party values things differently.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Labor-management negotiations that increase productivity in exchange for better wages can benefit both sides.

glossary_terms.definition: Setting an initial reference point in a negotiation that influences the final outcome.
glossary_terms.example: The first price mentioned in a negotiation becomes the anchor around which all counteroffers are compared.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research shows people are heavily influenced by the first number they hear, even when irrelevant.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Salary negotiations: starting with a high number tends to result in higher final offers.

coaching_moment: You're the new Chief Information Security Officer at India's largest private bank. Hackers are probing your defenses 24/7.
cultural_context: India ranks among the top targets for cyberattacks globally, with over 1.4 million incidents recorded annually. As India's digital economy grows, cybersecurity skills are among the most in-demand for Indian technology professionals.
reflection_prompt: How did you adapt as the AI shifted strategies? Which adaptation worked best?
